raw_case_text:
We report on a 32 year-old male with a history of contact eczema, residing at Djelfa town, in Algeria.
The patient reported a 6-week history of painless, and non-healing skin lesions on his right hand, he admitted having applied topical corticosteroids and antiseptics without any improvement, and then he had received two courses of antibiotics (pristinamycin, amoxicillin + clavulanic acid), with no significant results, moreover, there was an extension of the lesions leading to an imperative reevaluation of the condition. After being referred to our institution, the patient presented limited erythematous-papular plaque of 8 cm of diameter, located on the dorsal side of the right hand, the lesion was formed by the confluence of several papules (Fig. 1), with satellite lesions on the periphery, the initial plaque was associated with several firm and painless subcutaneous nodules 0.5-1.5 in diameter, following a lymphatic drainage to the elbow joint (Fig. 2). The patient didn't remembered being bitten by an insect, and other body surfaces did not reveal similar lesions. Furthermore examination of the other systems was unremarkable. Parasitological examination revealed abundant amastigote forms of Leishmania sp (Fig. 1), while direct mycological examination as well as the culture on Sabouraud medium at 25  C, and on the BHI medium (Brain Heart Infusion) at 37  C were both negative for fungal presence. In addition, culture on NNN medium (Novy- MacNeal-Nicolle), associated to species identification based on isoenzyme electrophoresis revealed Leishmania major as etiological agent.
The patient was started on Meglumine antimoniate (Glucantime ) as first line treatment 60 mg/kg/day for 15 days, which induced a reduction of the lesions after 10 days (Fig. 3), and favorable outcome at day 15 of follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 32-year-old Algerian man from Djelfa presented with a 6-week history of a painless, non-healing erythematous-papular plaque on the dorsum of his right hand accompanied by ascending subcutaneous nodules along the forearm.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 6 weeks prior to referral, the patient developed painless skin lesions on his right hand that continued to expand and ascend his forearm despite self-applied topical corticosteroids and antiseptics and two courses of oral antibiotics (pristinamycin and amoxicillin-clavulanic acid).
subjective.past_medical_history: History of contact eczema; resident of Djelfa town, Algeria (an endemic focus of cutaneous leishmaniasis); denied recalled insect bites.
subjective.review_of_systems: Negative for local pain or systemic symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: An 8-cm erythematous-papular plaque formed by confluent papules with peripheral satellite papules on the dorsal aspect of the right hand, accompanied by several firm, painless subcutaneous nodules (0.5-1.5 cm in diameter) ascending along the lymphatic drainage toward the elbow joint; remainder of physical examination was normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Direct mycological microscopy and fungal cultures on Sabouraud agar (25 C) and Brain Heart Infusion medium (37 C) were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Parasitological skin smears demonstrated abundant Leishmania sp. amastigotes, and culture on Novy-MacNeal-Nicolle (NNN) medium with isoenzyme electrophoresis identified Leishmania major.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis and bacterial lymphangitis were excluded by negative mycological cultures and lack of antibiotic response; direct skin smear microscopy and NNN culture with isoenzyme electrophoresis confirmed sporotrichoid Cutaneous Leishmaniasis caused by Leishmania major. First-line intramuscular meglumine antimoniate (Glucantime 60 mg/kg/day for 15 days) produced marked regression by day 10 and a favorable clinical outcome at day 15.
